headline: Chain-of-thought monitoring can fail even when the reasoning is necessary
summary: A 13 October 2026 preprint proposes four levels of chain-of-thought (CoT) necessity and reports that CoT monitoring can miss influential attributes even when the CoT is necessary to produce the answer. In intervention experiments with Qwen3 and Gemma4 models on benign classification tasks, the authors report near-zero monitorability scores for selected medical-task attributes; for Qwen3-8B on a thyroid-diagnosis class, patient sex and a thyroxine-history attribute systematically influenced at least 19% and 24% of correct CoT answers, respectively, yet were almost never identified as influential in the CoT. The paper presents this as evidence that answer-level CoT necessity alone does not guarantee monitorability. It does not test dangerous behavior or deployed frontier systems; the largest model is 31B parameters, the mechanism behind failures remains open, and the authors’ code repository says code will be released soon.
